docs.title: USMLE Agentic AI System
docs.text:
Multimodal Multi-Agent Adaptive Learning for USMLE Preparation

Welcome to the documentation for the Agentic AI USMLE Study Planning System—an intelligent, adaptive tutoring platform built with LangGraph, FastAPI, Supabase/pgvector, and multimodal RAG.

docs.title: What is This System?
docs.text:
This project implements a multimodal multi-agent AI orchestration system that:

  1. Diagnoses student strengths and weaknesses from NBME/UWorld performance reports
  2. Tracks knowledge vectors persistently across study sessions
  3. Retrieves relevant resources across 5 modalities (text, images, PDFs, video, audio) using RAG
  4. Generates adaptive, evidence-based study plans with specific resource recommendations

Unlike static AI tutoring systems, this platform maintains state, retrieves across modalities, and adapts over time—creating truly personalized learning experiences for International Medical Graduates (IMGs).

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Stateful Agentic Graph - LangGraph orchestration with memory checkpointing
  • Multimodal RAG - Retrieval across text, images (pathology, ECG, radiographs), PDFs, video (with timestamps), and audio
  • Evidence-Based Learning - Interleaved practice, spaced repetition, active recall
  • Persistent Knowledge Tracking - Supabase/pgvector-backed student knowledge vectors
  • IMG Optimization - Automatic boosting of IMG-specific resources (US healthcare system, lab values)
  • Human-in-the-Loop - Conditional review routing for clinical oversight
  • RESTful API - FastAPI with OpenAPI/Swagger documentation
  • Open Source - Fully documented for reproducible research

docs.title: Retrieval Algorithm
docs.text:
def retrieve(
    query_area: str,
    query_topic: str,
    max_results: int = 10,
    modalities: Optional[List[Modality]] = None,
    min_tier: ResourceTier = ResourceTier.SUPPLEMENTARY,
    img_specific_bonus: bool = False
) -> List[MultimodalResource]:

Scoring components: 1. Area match (+5.0 exact, +3.0 partial) 2. Topic match in description (+3.0) and topic field (+2.0) 3. Tag matches (+1.0 each) 4. Modality preference bonus (+2.0) 5. Tier priority (+0.5 to +2.5) 6. Student rating bonus (up to +1.5) 7. IMG-specific bonus (+1.5) 8. Usage popularity bonus (+0.5)

docs.title: Multimodal Set Retrieval
docs.text:
def retrieve_multimodal_set(
    area: str,
    topic: str,
    target_hours: float,
    learning_style: Optional[str] = None,
    is_img_student: bool = False
) -> Dict[str, List[MultimodalResource]]:

Ensures balanced modality coverage: 1. Text: Always included (primary reference) 2. Image: Included for visual learners or when time allows 3. Video: Included for conceptual understanding 4. QBank: Always included for active recall 5. IMG-specific: Included for IMG students 6. PDF: Included if high-yield reference available

docs.title: Multimodal Resources Table
docs.text:
The core of the RAG system:

CREATE TABLE multimodal_resources (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    resource_id VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE,  -- e.g., "fa-txt-cardio"
    name VARCHAR(255),
    source VARCHAR(100),              -- "First Aid", "UWorld", "Pathoma"
    modality resource_modality,       -- text, pdf, image, video, audio
    area VARCHAR(100),
    topic VARCHAR(200),
    description TEXT,
    tier resource_tier,               -- essential, high-yield, supplementary, reference

    -- Content
    content_text TEXT,                -- Text content / transcript
    content_url TEXT,                 -- File path or URL
    page_range VARCHAR(50),           -- "pp. 265-280"
    timestamp_range VARCHAR(50),      -- "12:30-18:45"

    -- Embeddings
    text_embedding vector(1536),      -- OpenAI ada-002
    image_embedding vector(768),      -- CLIP ViT-L/14

    -- Image metadata
    image_type VARCHAR(50),           -- pathology_slide, ECG, radiograph, diagram, table
    image_description TEXT,

    -- Video metadata
    video_url TEXT,
    duration_minutes DECIMAL(5,1),
    key_frames TEXT[],                -- ["00:00 Topic 1", "30:00 Topic 2"]

    -- Engagement
    estimated_hours DECIMAL(3,1),
    student_rating DECIMAL(2,1),
    usage_count INTEGER,

    -- Tags
    tags TEXT[],
    img_specific BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE
);

docs.title: Vector Indexes
docs.text:
-- Text similarity (IVFFlat for approximate nearest neighbor)
CREATE INDEX idx_resources_text_embedding 
    ON multimodal_resources USING ivfflat (text_embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Image similarity
CREATE INDEX idx_resources_image_embedding 
    ON multimodal_resources USING ivfflat (image_embedding vector_cosine_ops);

docs.title: Row Level Security
docs.text:
RLS policies ensure data isolation:

-- Students can only access their own data
CREATE POLICY "Students can view own data" ON students
    FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid()::text = external_id);

-- Resource catalog is publicly readable
CREATE POLICY "Anyone can view resources" ON multimodal_resources
    FOR SELECT USING (true);

-- Students can track their resource interactions
CREATE POLICY "Students can insert own interactions" ON student_resource_interactions
    FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (student_id IN (
        SELECT id FROM students WHERE external_id = auth.uid()::text
    ));

docs.title: Stage 1: Topic Scoring
docs.text:
Every resource is scored using:

score = (
    5.0 if exact_area_match else
    3.0 if partial_area_match else 0
    + 3.0 if topic_in_description
    + 2.0 if topic_in_topic_field
    + sum(1.0 for matching_tag)
    + tier_bonus (0.5-2.5)
    + student_rating/5 * 1.5
    + 1.5 if img_specific and is_img_student
    + 0.5 if usage_count > 10
)

docs.title: Stage 2: Modality Balancing
docs.text: Ensures at least one resource from each category: - Primary text: Core reference (First Aid chapter or UWorld explanations) - Visual: Image or diagram for visual learners - Video: Lecture segment for conceptual understanding - QBank: Practice questions for active recall - IMG: IMG-specific resource when applicable

docs.title: Stage 3: Constraint Filtering
docs.text:
• Filters by available study time
  • Respects learning style preferences
  • Ensures tier minimums (at least "high-yield" quality)

docs.title: Stage 4: Ranking
docs.text: Returns top resources sorted by combined relevance score.

docs.title: System Architecture Overview
docs.text: The Agentic USMLE system implements a stateful multimodal multi-agent graph where specialized AI agents communicate through a typed state object.

docs.title: Four-Agent Design
docs.text: Agent Responsibility Input Output A: Diagnostician Parse performance reports Raw report text Structured assessment B: Knowledge Manager Maintain knowledge vectors Diagnostic + performance Updated proficiencies C: Resource Optimizer Multimodal RAG retrieval Knowledge state + topics Resource recommendations across text, images, PDFs, video, audio D: Adaptive Scheduler Generate study plans Knowledge + resources Multimodal study plan

docs.title: Multimodal RAG Pipeline
docs.text:
The Resource Optimizer (Agent C) implements a 4-stage retrieval pipeline:

1. Topic Scoring → Score all 45+ resources by topic match
2. Modality Balancing → Ensure text + image + video + qbank coverage
3. Constraint Filtering → Filter by time, learning style, IMG status
4. Ranking → Sort by combined relevance (topic + tier + ratings + popularity)

docs.title: Supported Modalities
docs.text: Modality Examples Embedding Model Dimensions Text First Aid chapters, UWorld explanations OpenAI ada-002 1536 Images Pathology slides, ECG strips, radiographs, diagrams CLIP ViT-L/14 768 PDFs NBME reports, study guides, practice exams OpenAI ada-002 (extracted text) 1536 Video Pathoma, B&B lectures with timestamps OpenAI ada-002 (metadata/transcripts) 1536 Audio Podcast episodes, lecture recordings OpenAI ada-002 (transcripts) 1536

docs.title: 1. Stateful Orchestration
docs.text:
• Memory checkpointing via LangGraph's MemorySaver
  • Database persistence for all student data and agent outputs
  • Execution logging for debugging and research

docs.title: 2. Agent Specialization
docs.text: Each agent has a narrow, well-defined responsibility enabling independent optimization and evaluation.

docs.title: 3. Conditional Routing
docs.text: Intelligent branching routes low-confidence or high-risk students to human review.

docs.title: 4. Fallback Mechanisms
docs.text: Every agent has a fallback (mock diagnostic, heuristic plans, text-only resources) ensuring reliability.

docs.title: 5. IMG Optimization
docs.text: Automatic boosting of IMG-specific resources (US healthcare system, lab values, clinical context) for identified IMG students.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide walks through setting up the Agentic USMLE system for development or research use.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+ (3.11 recommended)
  • Supabase account (free tier sufficient)
  • Groq API key (free tier available)
  • Git for version control

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/stanley-nelavala/Agentic-AI-for-USMLE-Prep.git
cd Agentic-AI-for-USMLE-Prep

docs.title: Step 2: Create Virtual Environment
docs.text:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

docs.title: Step 3: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt

Or using pyproject.toml:

pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file:

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env with your credentials:

# Groq API
GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_your_key_here
GROQ_MODEL=llama-3.1-70b-versatile

# Supabase
SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your_service_role_key

docs.title: Obtaining API Keys
docs.text:
Groq API Key: 1. Sign up at console.groq.com 2. Create an API key in the dashboard 3. Free tier includes 10K requests/day

Supabase Credentials: 1. Create a project at supabase.com 2. Go to Project Settings → API 3. Copy your project URL and service role key

docs.title: Step 5: Initialize Database
docs.text:
Run the SQL schema in your Supabase SQL editor:

  1. Open your Supabase project
  2. Navigate to SQL Editor
  3. Copy and paste contents of src/database/schema.sql
  4. Run the migration from src/database/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql

docs.title: Step 6: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Test the database connection:

python -c "from src.database.client import test_connection; print(test_connection())"

Run the API server:

uvicorn src.api.app:app --reload

Visit http://localhost:8000/docs to see the API documentation.

docs.title: Step 7: Run a Test Assessment
docs.text:
python -m src.agents.main --student-id IMG001 --json

This will run the complete agent pipeline with mock data.

docs.title: Groq API Not Configured
docs.text: If GROQ_API_KEY is not set, the system will fall back to mock diagnostics. This is fine for testing.

docs.title: Supabase Connection Error
docs.text: Verify your URL and key are correct. Check that the schema has been applied.

docs.title: Import Errors
docs.text: Ensure you're in the project root directory and the virtual environment is activated.

docs.title: Evaluation Framework
docs.text: Scripts and methodology for analyzing system performance and user study data.

docs.title: Pipeline Execution Tests
docs.text:
Run the evaluation suite:

python evaluation/technical_evaluation.py

This script: 1. Generates 100 simulated student profiles 2. Runs the complete agent pipeline for each 3. Collects execution metrics 4. Outputs summary statistics

docs.title: Metrics Collected
docs.text: Metric Description Target execution_time_ms Total pipeline time < 10,000ms success_rate Percentage of successful runs > 95% diagnostic_accuracy Weak area identification accuracy > 80% plan_quality Rubric score (expert review) > 0.8/1.0

docs.title: Pre/Post Score Comparison
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load data
data = pd.read_csv("data/user_study_results.csv")

# Paired t-test
t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_rel(data['post_score'], data['pre_score'])

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohen_d = (data['post_score'].mean() - data['pre_score'].mean()) / data['pre_score'].std()

print(f"t({len(data)-1}) = {t_stat:.2f}, p = {p_value:.3f}")
print(f"Cohen's d = {cohen_d:.2f}")

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text:
# Score trajectory
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.scatter(data['pre_score'], data['post_score'], alpha=0.7)
plt.plot([140, 260], [140, 260], 'r--', alpha=0.5)  # Diagonal
plt.xlabel('Pre-study NBME Score')
plt.ylabel('Post-study NBME Score')
plt.title('Score Improvement')
plt.savefig('evaluation/score_improvement.png')

Interview themes:

# Example theme coding
themes = {

docs.title: Plan Quality Rubric (Blessie's Framework)
docs.text:
Score each criterion 0-1:

Criterion 0 (Poor) 0.5 (Partial) 1 (Excellent) Weak area prioritization Ignores weak areas Some focus on weak areas Heavy focus on weakest topics Interleaving quality All blocked practice Some mixing Optimal interleaving Spaced repetition No review scheduling Review present but irregular Evidence-based intervals IMG appropriateness Generic advice Some IMG consideration Addresses IMG-specific gaps Feasibility Unrealistic hours Mostly feasible Well-calibrated to student

docs.title: Inter-Rater Reliability
docs.text:
If multiple experts score plans:

from scipy.stats import pearsonr

rater1 = [0.9, 0.8, 0.95, ...]
rater2 = [0.85, 0.82, 0.90, ...]

correlation, p_value = pearsonr(rater1, rater2)
print(f"Inter-rater reliability: r = {correlation:.2f}")

docs.title: Statistical Power
docs.text:
For the pilot study (n=10-20):

  • Effect size detectable: d = 0.8 (large) with n=15, α=0.05, power=0.80
  • Recommendation: Treat pilot as exploratory; definitive RCT needs n=100+

docs.title: Reporting Results
docs.text:
Follow JMIR guidelines:

  1. Report exact p-values (not just < 0.05)
  2. Include confidence intervals for effect sizes
  3. Describe missing data
  4. Report both statistical and practical significance

docs.title: Example Report
docs.text:
## Results

### Primary Outcome

Students improved by an average of 12.3 points (SD = 8.5) on NBME practice exams after 4 weeks of agentic-guided study, t(14) = 5.42, p < 0.001, 95% CI [7.8, 16.8]. The effect size was large (Cohen's d = 1.45).

### Secondary Outcomes

- Average system usage: 4.2 sessions/week (SD = 1.8)
- Plans generated: 3.1 per student (SD = 1.2)
- Plan helpfulness rating: 4.2/5.0 (SD = 0.6)

### Qualitative Themes

Three major themes emerged:
1. **Structured guidance** (12/15 participants): "Finally knew what to study each day"
2. **Weak area focus** (10/15): "Made me study things I was avoiding"
3. **Confidence building** (8/15): "Seeing my predicted score go up helped"

docs.title: Researcher's Handbook: Methodology
docs.text: This document describes the research methodology for evaluating the Agentic USMLE system.

docs.title: Research Questions
docs.text:
1. RQ1: Does agentic AI-generated study planning improve USMLE practice exam scores compared to self-directed study?
  2. RQ2: How does the quality of LLM-generated plans compare to heuristic-based plans as evaluated by clinical experts?
  3. RQ3: What is the feasibility and reliability of the agentic pipeline in production conditions?

docs.title: Phase 1: Technical Evaluation (Completed)
docs.text:
Objective: Validate system functionality and performance.

Methods: - 100 test runs with simulated student data - Measure execution time, success rate, plan quality - Compare LLM vs. heuristic plan generation

Metrics: - Pipeline execution time (target: < 10 seconds) - Success rate (target: > 95%) - Plan quality rubric score (target: > 0.8/1.0)

docs.title: Phase 2: Expert Review (In Progress)
docs.text:
Objective: Clinical validation of generated plans.

Methods: - Blessie (clinical advisor) evaluates 30 plans using rubric - Compare against manually created "gold standard" plans - Qualitative feedback on plan appropriateness

Rubric (5 criteria, 0-1 scale each): 1. Weak area prioritization 2. Interleaving quality 3. Spaced repetition implementation 4. IMG-specific appropriateness 5. Feasibility (time allocation)

docs.title: Phase 3: Pilot User Study (Planned)
docs.text:
Objective: Real-world evaluation with IMG students.

Participants: 10-20 IMGs preparing for USMLE Step 1

Inclusion Criteria: - IMG (non-US medical school graduate) - Planning to take Step 1 within 6 months - Baseline NBME score < 200 - Willing to use system for minimum 2 weeks

Procedure: 1. Pre-study: Baseline NBME practice exam 2. Weeks 1-2: Use system for study planning 3. Mid-study: Usage metrics collection 4. Weeks 3-4: Continue system use 5. Post-study: NBME practice exam, qualitative interview

Outcome Measures: - Primary: NBME score change (pre vs. post) - Secondary: System usage (sessions, plans generated) - Qualitative: Plan helpfulness, personalization, usability

docs.title: Student Onboarding Guide
docs.text: Welcome to the Agentic USMLE Study Planning System! This guide will help you get started.

docs.title: What is This System?
docs.text:
This is an AI-powered study planning tool designed specifically for International Medical Graduates (IMGs) preparing for USMLE Step 1.

Unlike commercial question banks that just give you practice questions, this system:

  1. Analyzes your NBME/UWorld performance reports
  2. Identifies your specific weak areas
  3. Creates a personalized study schedule using evidence-based strategies
  4. Adapts your plan based on your progress

docs.title: Who Should Use This?
docs.text:
• IMGs preparing for USMLE Step 1
  • Students with baseline NBME scores between 160-220
  • Anyone who wants a structured, adaptive study plan
  • Students willing to share their performance data for research

docs.title: Step 1: Provide Your Information
docs.text:
You'll need to share:

  1. Student ID: A unique identifier (e.g., IMG001)
  2. NBME Score: Your most recent practice exam score (if available)
  3. UWorld Percentile: Your current UWorld performance percentile (if available)
  4. Target Exam Date: When you plan to take the actual USMLE
  5. Daily Study Hours: How many hours per day you can study

docs.title: Step 2: Upload Your Performance Report
docs.text:
You can provide: - Text summary of your NBME/UWorld performance - Specific weak/strong areas you're aware of - Recent practice question session results

Example report format:

NBME 25 Score: 185
UWorld Percentile: 45%

Weak Areas:
- Cardiology: 60% correct on practice questions
- Biochemistry: 50% correct
- Pharmacology: 55% correct

Strong Areas:
- Anatomy: 80% correct
- Physiology: 75% correct

Available study time: 6 hours/day
Target exam date: September 15, 2026

docs.title: Step 3: Receive Your Study Plan
docs.text:
Within seconds, the system will generate:

  1. Diagnostic Assessment: Analysis of your strengths/weaknesses
  2. Knowledge Profile: Your current predicted USMLE score
  3. Study Plan: A detailed 7-day schedule with specific topics and practice questions

docs.title: Plan Structure
docs.text:
Your plan will include:

Component Description Study Blocks Individual study sessions (2-4 per day) Topics Specific topics to focus on (not just "Cardiology" but "Heart Failure") Practice Questions Number of questions to complete per block Review Type How to study: active recall, spaced repetition, interleaved, or full review Resources Recommended materials (UWorld, First Aid, Pathoma, etc.)

docs.title: Example Day
docs.text:
Day 1: Monday, April 7, 2026

Block 1 (2.5 hours): Cardiology - Heart Failure
- Type: Active Recall
- Practice Questions: 30
- Resources: UWorld, First Aid, Pathoma

Block 2 (2.0 hours): Anatomy - Thorax
- Type: Interleaved
- Practice Questions: 20
- Resources: UWorld, Amboss

Block 3 (1.5 hours): Physiology - High-yield Review
- Type: Spaced Repetition
- Practice Questions: 12
- Resources: Anki, First Aid Rapid Review

docs.title: Every 3rd Day: Review Day
docs.text: Every third day will be a comprehensive review day: - Morning: Intensive review of your weakest area - Afternoon: Mixed practice questions (simulates exam conditions)

docs.title: Evidence-Based Strategies Used
docs.text: Your plan implements three proven learning strategies:

docs.title: 1. Interleaved Practice
docs.text:
Instead of studying one topic all day, your plan mixes different subjects. Research shows this improves long-term retention by 25-40%.

Why? It forces your brain to discriminate between different types of problems—exactly what the USMLE does.

docs.title: 2. Spaced Repetition
docs.text:
Review sessions are scheduled at optimal intervals to prevent forgetting. You'll review material just before you're about to forget it.

Why? The "forgetting curve" is steepest in the first few days. Spaced review flattens it.

docs.title: 3. Active Recall
docs.text:
Every block includes practice questions. Testing yourself is more effective than re-reading notes.

Why? Retrieval strengthens memory traces more than passive review.

docs.title: Knowledge Vector
docs.text:
The system maintains a "knowledge vector" tracking your proficiency in each area:

Cardiology: 35% → 42% → 48% → 55%
Biochemistry: 40% → 45% → 50% → 52%
Anatomy: 75% → 76% → 78% → 80%

Watch your proficiencies increase over time!

docs.title: Predicted Score
docs.text:
Based on your knowledge state, the system predicts your USMLE score:

Week 1: 182
Week 2: 188
Week 3: 194
Week 4: 201  ← Passing threshold is ~196

docs.title: Providing Feedback
docs.text:
After using your plan for a few days, tell us:

  1. Was the plan helpful? (1-5 scale)
  2. Did it address your weaknesses? (Yes/Partial/No)
  3. Were the daily hours realistic? (Yes/No)
  4. What would you change? (Open feedback)

Your feedback helps improve the system for future students!

docs.title: Privacy & Data Use
docs.text:
• Your data is stored securely in Supabase
  • Only you and the research team can access your data
  • Individual scores are never shared publicly
  • Aggregate data may be used in research publications (anonymized)

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
If you have questions or issues:

  • Technical issues: Contact Stanley (technical lead)
  • Study advice: Contact Blessie (clinical advisor)
  • General questions: Check this documentation

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
1. Review the Using Your Plan Guide for tips
  2. Run your first assessment via the API or CLI
  3. Start following your generated plan
  4. Report back after 1 week with your experience

Good luck with your USMLE preparation! 🎓

docs.title: Using Your Study Plan
docs.text: Tips for getting the most out of your AI-generated USMLE study plan.

docs.title: Before Each Block
docs.text:
1. Review the block details: Note the topic, duration, and question target
  2. Gather resources: Have UWorld, First Aid, and other materials ready
  3. Set a timer: Stick to the allocated hours

docs.title: During the Block
docs.text:
1. Start with practice questions (active recall first!)
  2. Review explanations for both correct and incorrect answers
  3. Take notes on concepts you missed
  4. Use the Pomodoro technique: 50 min study, 10 min break

docs.title: After Each Block
docs.text:
1. Log your performance: Record questions attempted/correct
  2. Note confidence level: How well did you feel? (1-5 scale)
  3. Mark completed: Update the system so it can adapt your plan

docs.title: Review Day Strategy
docs.text: Every 3rd day is a comprehensive review day. Here's how to maximize it:

docs.title: Morning Session (Weak Area Intensive)
docs.text:
• Focus on your lowest proficiency area
  • Review all incorrect UWorld questions from the past week
  • Re-read First Aid sections on missed topics
  • Target: 50-60 practice questions

docs.title: Afternoon Session (Mixed Practice)
docs.text:
• Do 40-60 mixed questions (simulates exam conditions)
  • Don't look up answers until you've completed the block
  • Review all explanations thoroughly
  • Track your accuracy by topic

docs.title: When a Topic is Too Hard
docs.text:
If you're scoring < 40% on practice questions:

  1. Don't panic—this is exactly why the system identified it as a weak area!
  2. Spend extra time on foundational concepts
  3. Use additional resources (Pathoma videos, Boards & Beyond)
  4. The system will notice and adjust your next plan accordingly

docs.title: When a Topic is Too Easy
docs.text:
If you're scoring > 85% consistently:

  1. Move faster through the material
  2. Focus on details you might be missing
  3. The system will reduce time allocation in future plans

docs.title: Missing a Study Day
docs.text:
Life happens. If you miss a day:

  1. Don't try to "catch up" by doubling the next day
  2. Resume with the current day's plan
  3. The system will reschedule missed content in future plans
  4. Log what you actually studied (even if it wasn't the plan)

docs.title: High-Yield Strategies
docs.text:
1. Prioritize UWorld: It's the single best resource. Do every question at least once.
  2. Review incorrects thoroughly: Understanding why you missed a question is more valuable than getting it right.
  3. Use First Aid as a reference: Don't read it cover-to-cover; use it to look up concepts you miss.
  4. Take NBME practice exams: Every 2 weeks to track progress.

docs.title: IMG-Specific Tips
docs.text:
1. US Healthcare System: Dedicate extra time to ethics, preventive medicine, and biostatistics
  2. Clinical Vignettes: Practice reading long question stems quickly
  3. Drug Names: Focus on US brand names (not just generic/international names)
  4. Lab Values: Memorize US reference ranges (may differ from your country)

docs.title: Weekly Check-In
docs.text:
Every week, ask yourself:

Question Rating (1-5) Did I follow the plan consistently? Did my practice question accuracy improve? Do I feel more confident in weak areas? Is the daily hour allocation realistic?

docs.title: Monthly Milestones
docs.text:
• Week 1-2: Establish study routine, identify resource preferences
  • Week 3-4: Notice improvement in weak areas, adjust study strategies
  • Week 5-6: Take NBME practice exam, compare to baseline
  • Week 7-8: Refine plan based on NBME results, continue cycle

docs.title: Q: How many hours should I study per day?
docs.text: A: 6-8 hours is typical for dedicated study. The system adapts to your available time. Quality > quantity—focused, active study for 6 hours beats distracted studying for 10.

docs.title: Q: Should I do UWorld timed or tutor mode?
docs.text: A: - Weeks 1-2: Tutor mode (learn at your pace) - Weeks 3+: Timed (simulates exam pressure) - Review days: Always timed

docs.title: Q: What if I disagree with the plan's prioritization?
docs.text: A: The plan is a recommendation. If you know a specific topic needs more/less time, adjust accordingly. Log what you actually studied so the system learns your preferences.

docs.title: Q: How often should I take NBME practice exams?
docs.text: A: Every 2 weeks. More frequently doesn't give you time to improve; less frequently loses tracking resolution.

docs.title: Q: Can I use this for Step 2 CK?
docs.text: A: Currently, the system is optimized for Step 1. Step 2 CK support is planned for future versions.

docs.title: Problem: Plan feels too overwhelming
docs.text: Solution: Reduce daily hours in your profile. The system will create shorter, more focused blocks.

docs.title: Problem: I'm not improving in my weak area
docs.text: Solution: 1. Check if you're actually doing the practice questions 2. Try different resources (maybe Pathoma works better than First Aid for you) 3. The system should automatically increase time allocation—verify this in your next plan

docs.title: Problem: The plan doesn't account for my clinical rotations
docs.text: Solution: Update your available study hours. If you only have 4 hours/day during rotations, tell the system.

docs.title: Success Stories
docs.text:
"I never would have mixed Cardiology with Biochemistry on the same day, but the interleaving actually made me retain both better."

— Pilot participant, IMG from India

"The plan told me exactly which Heart Failure subtopics to focus on, not just 'study Cardiology.' That specificity was game-changing."

— Pilot participant, IMG from Philippines

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Log your study sessions consistently
  • Take an NBME practice exam every 2 weeks
  • Provide feedback on plan helpfulness
  • Share your experience with the research team

Stay consistent, trust the process, and good luck! 🎯
